author: NorthEast News Desk
body: UFC heavyweight champion Tom Aspinall has vacated his title while recovering from complications tied to an eye injury, the British fighter said Monday, according to Reuters.

Aspinall underwent multiple surgeries after eye injuries during his title defense against Ciryl Gane in Abu Dhabi last October. That bout was ruled a first-round no contest after he could not continue.

The 33-year-old said he decided to give up the belt rather than hold up the division. He had agreed to a fight date and resumed sparring before another accident caused additional damage to his right eye, Reuters reported.

The move clears the way for Gane, who won an interim heavyweight title by beating Alex Pereira in June, to be elevated to undisputed champion. UFC officials had not announced a new fight date for Aspinall.
Aspinall said he is not retiring and hopes to return after he is healthy and medically cleared. His departure leaves the division with a new champion while his recovery timeline remains uncertain.
dek: The British fighter says ongoing complications and another accident made him relinquish the title, but he is not retiring.
headline: Tom Aspinall gives up UFC heavyweight belt while recovering from eye injury
